basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Treats the decision as an inspectable knowledge object: issue, alternatives, criteria, outcome and rationale.
Unlike the approval activity, it records what was decided and why, not how the meeting ran.
Unlike a legal judgment, it is not itself a binding legal instrument.
Unlike an executable rule, it does not evaluate or enforce anything.

may: Frame a decision and register alternatives.
Declare criteria and weights and evaluate alternatives.
Bind reasons to claims and evidence citations.
Re-check assumptions and flag when they change.
mustNot: Record a decision as approved without recorded authority.
Change an approved version in place.
Erase decision content when supersession or tombstoning is required.
Present its own analysis as the decision made.
Copy content owned by referenced models.
requiresHuman: Revoking or superseding an approved decision.

considerations: People affected by decisions have an interest in knowing the reasons.
Rationale records can reveal the views of named participants and need careful access.
Alternatives rejected for biased reasons should be visible to review.

items: A decision record has an issue, alternatives, criteria, a selected outcome, authority and a date.
Often confused with meeting minutes, a policy rule, a legal judgment and a change request.
Decisions reopened or misapplied because rationale is missing.
